title: NY State Assembly · District 56

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Stefani Zinerman did not win renomination. In the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, Eon Tyrell Huntley defeated Zinerman and Michael Bailey with 58.3% of the vote. The Republican primary was canceled with no candidate advancing, and Huntley also advanced from the Working Families Party primary without appearing on the ballot, leaving him unopposed in the November 3 general election.

candidates.name: Eon Tyrell Huntley
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating incumbent Stefani Zinerman

summary.text: Eon Tyrell Huntley describes himself as a father, retail worker, lifelong Brooklynite, democratic socialist and three-term PTA president. He ran unsuccessfully in the 2024 Democratic primary for Assembly District 56, then defeated incumbent Stefani Zinerman in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary and is unopposed in the November general election. His campaign website lists universal childcare, a rent freeze and expanded rent controls among his priorities.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and campaign website, Huntley grew up in East New York and in NYCHA's Pink Houses; his father immigrated from Guyana and his mother is a second-generation Brooklynite.

Ballotpedia lists a high school diploma from the High School of Art and Design and a bachelor's degree from the Parsons School of Design in 2006. He also says he attended New York City public schools.
He describes working as a fashion designer and, currently, a retail clothing salesman; Ballotpedia lists his profession as retail.
He says that as a member of the bargaining committee for Workers United Local 340, he fought for and won healthcare coverage for fellow workers.
He says he served three terms as PTA president at his daughters' school and co-founded a mobile food pantry that fed hundreds of Brooklyn residents each month during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Huntley ran in the June 25, 2024 Democratic primary for Assembly District 56 and lost to incumbent Stefani Zinerman, 46.9% to 52.8%.

On June 23, 2026 he defeated Zinerman and a third candidate, Michael Bailey, in the Democratic primary with 58.3% of the vote, and he also advanced on the Working Families Party line after that party's primary was canceled.
In his survey he says he has lived in Bedford-Stuyvesant for 19 years with his wife Rebecca, a public school teacher.

priorities.text: "We must pass the Universal Child Care Act to guarantee the best possible start for every child. This act will invest in building out our state's childcare infrastructure and put us on the path toward a truly universal system, where every family in our state has quality care, nobody gets priced or means-tested out, and childcare workers are treated with dignity and compensated generously."

"Housing is a human right... Eon supports Mayor Mamdani's rent freeze and wants to expand tenant protections and freeze rents across New York State. He believes in decommodifying housing, standing up to bad landlords, and dramatically increasing funding for NYCHA," including support for Assemblymember Gallagher's plan to create a Social Housing Development Authority.

"Eon believes an injury to one is an injury to all... he has always advocated for severing all ties between New York State and ICE, including a moratorium on immigrant detention facilities in our state."

researchNotes: Huntley is unopposed on the Nov 3, 2026 general-election ballot. He has not held elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record. Priorities and positions are drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response (submitted September 5, 2026), which is his own account of his platform; a separate campaign website (eonforassembly.com) largely repeats the same language. Huntley's biography is drawn from his own Candidate Connection survey and campaign website (self-described); no independent news profile was used.
